frontmatter.title: What Is Tech Neck, and Can a Pillow Help?
frontmatter.description: Tech neck is strain from looking down at screens. What causes it, the daytime habits that help most, what a pillow can do, and when to see a doctor.
frontmatter.seo_answer: Tech neck, or text neck, is a popular name for neck and shoulder strain from looking down at phones, tablets and laptops for long periods. It is not a formal diagnosis, and studies disagree on how much phone posture alone causes pain. The changes that matter most happen during the day: raise screens towards eye level, take regular breaks, and keep your neck and upper back moving. A pillow cannot undo tech neck, but one that keeps your neck aligned overnight avoids adding more strain while you sleep.

frontmatter.description: What a pillow, a bolster and a body pillow each support, how the three compare, and how to sleep correctly with a body pillow.
frontmatter.seo_answer: A pillow and a bolster do different jobs, so side sleepers often benefit from both. The pillow fills the space between your head and the mattress, so your neck stays level. A bolster or body pillow supports the rest of you. Hugged in front, it rests your top arm; tucked between your knees, it keeps your hips level. A body pillow is longer than a bolster and often C- or U-shaped. If you sleep on your back without pain, a well-fitted pillow may be all you need.

frontmatter.title: How to Use a Bolster for Back and Hip Comfort in Pregnancy
frontmatter.description: Positioning a bolster for side sleeping in later pregnancy, what NHS and ACOG guidance says, what to look for, and when to call your midwife.
frontmatter.seo_answer: Lie on your side with your knees bent and a bolster between them. Your top leg should rest level with your hip, instead of pulling your pelvis forward. Add a small cushion under your bump, and a pillow behind your back if you tend to roll. NHS and ACOG guidance is to sleep on your side in later pregnancy, and either side is fine. A bolster can make that position more comfortable. It does not address the cause of back or pelvic pain. Tell your midwife or doctor about pain that is severe or does not settle.
